text:
sam: quick ping — PR #7744 is green except for a small mem bump in longseq smoke on canary. attaching bench summary.

jess: :eyes: which canary? prod or canary-2?

sam: canary-2. benchmark run: 1000 iters with seq_len=4096 on p4d. results:
```
throughput: baseline 120 tok/s -> pr 118 tok/s (-1.7%)
p95 latency: baseline 310ms -> pr 345ms (+11%)
mem rss: baseline 42.1GB -> pr 45.6GB (+8.3%)
```

liam: hmm p95 up 11% is notable. is that the single-threaded microbatch test or full serving harness?

sam: full serving harness with KV cache warm. microbatch microbench (single replica) shows negligible throughput diff: `python bench.py --iters 500` baseline 210 tok/s, pr 208 tok/s.

aya: could the rss increase be from additional tensor materialization in the new allocator path? PR touches alloc fast-path.

jess: @liam @aya can you take a quick look at the alloc diffs? if it's just peak RSS but tail latency stable we might merge with a follow-up rollback plan.

liam: looking now. I can reproduce the RSS delta locally; leaving logs in gist: https://gist.github.com/xxxx

deploy-bot: canary deploy started for pr-7744 on canary-2 at 2025-06-12T14:10:00Z

sam: thanks. plan: hold merge until one of two: 1) confirm alloc tweak fixes RSS, or 2) agree canary fallback policy covers this and schedule merge after 2 successful canary windows. pref for (1).

jess: agree. @liam assign me when you have a minimal repro.

liam: will do, ETA ~45m.

aya: quick note — I added a guard to cap kv cache growth in latest commit in this branch, might shave the 3-4GB. re-running.

sam: great. if we can get mem back within 3% and p95 back <5% delta we can merge after one successful canary. otherwise we hold and escalate.

jess: tagging product for visibility: @product

sam: updating the PR description with these numbers and the canary plan. :thumbsup:
